name: Still Point
description: Held keys are warm steady tones. One sine sweeps slowly back and forth through them, so the beat with each key slows to stillness as they meet, then speeds away.

params.name: Time
params.description: Seconds the sine takes for one pass from its lowest point to its highest. A longer pass makes every meeting with a key slower.

params.name: Reach
params.description: How far past the lowest and the highest held key the sine travels before it turns. Small keeps the beat slow, large makes it fast at each end.

params.name: Level
params.description: Level of the sine against one key. At half it sits 6 dB under, and a meeting can dip the key by that much. At full the two can cancel for a moment.

params.name: Ears
params.description: Splits keys and sine between the ears: at full the keys are in the left ear and the sine in the right. Speakers, a mono fold or a shared reverb put the beat in the air.

params.name: Warmth
params.description: Adds the second, third and fourth partials to the held tones, from a pure sine to a fuller tone. The sweeping sine stays pure.

params.name: Attack
params.description: How long a key takes to fade in. The sine fades in with the loudest key.

params.name: Release
params.description: How long a key takes to fade out once it is let go. The sine fades with the last key and stops when that key has gone.

params.name: Volume
params.description: Output level of the instrument. A soft clip after it guards the output and does nothing to a full pool of keys at the default level.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit and cpp/kit/beat.h. Up to eight held keys are steady tones (a sine with second, third and fourth partials set by Warmth), and one pure sine sweeps in pitch as a triangle on a double clock between Reach semitones below the lowest held key and Reach above the highest, so the beat between the sine and each key slows to nothing where they meet. Choices, not measurements of anything: the partials at 0.5, 0.3 and 0.15 of the fundamental at full Warmth, in phases that keep the peak low; the limits follow the held keys through a one pole of 0.8 s; the sine's level follows the loudest key; the keys are scaled by the root of their summed power so a full pool stays under the soft clip's knee at the default volume; a key struck again while held carries on in its own voice, and a second voice on the same pitch starts in phase with the first. The sweep, the sine and the smoothing restart at the sample where a key arrives with no voice sounding.
